Definition: to be weak, i.e. (figuratively) to despond (causatively, rebuke), or (of light, the eye) to grow dull
BiblicalUsage: Kahah is growing dim — eyes that fail, strength that fades, a spirit that sinks. Isaac's eyes were dim so that he could not see; Moses died with his eye not dim and his natural force unabated; and Isaiah promises that the Servant shall not fail nor be discouraged till He has set judgment in the earth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word draws the line between age and despair. Eyes dim with years, but the Servant does not grow dim — and that is why I look to Him when my own strength fades, because His does not.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
